text:
Anna: heads-up — did an nsys run on the KV-cache regression and I think our sampling window was too short, we missed several short-lived kernel launches.
Anna: CLI I used:
Anna: ```bash
nsys profile --output=kv-issue --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=8 --force-overwrite --capture-range=duration:0:8 ./run_inference.sh
```
Anna: timeline looks mostly empty for the 2–3ms kernels, only big memcpy and osrt markers show up.
Sam: 8s is pretty short when OSRT sampling defaults to small windows. did you capture multiple requests or just one load-test run?
Anna: single steady run at 8 concurrent requests, sustained for ~6s after warmup.
Maya: quick thought — if kernels are <5ms and we only capture a few samples, sampling will skip them. try increasing duration to at least 20s or disable sampling for small runs.
Maya: example I usually run:
Maya: ```bash
nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=30 ./perf_run.sh
```
Maya: or for sampling-sensitive stuff use `--sample=none` so nsys records all OSRT markers and NVTX but beware output size.
Ron: also confirm OSRT sample window settings on our build. OSRT has an internal sample-window that controls aggregation frequency — if it's set to 64ms we will miss many sub-10ms kernels in the aggregate view.
Ron: someone should grep for env var OSRT_SAMPLE_WINDOW or check the runtime defaults in metrics.h
Anna: I dug into the binary — there is a compile-time default of 64 and a runtime override via RED_SAMPLING_WINDOW env var on our fork. I reproduced by setting RED_SAMPLING_WINDOW=16 and the small kernels show up as distinct events.
perf-bot: automated run: link to artifact (s3://redwood-perf/kv/1812345678/trace.qd3) :package: :eyes:
Sam: nice find. So short-term: increase nsys duration and set RED_SAMPLING_WINDOW=16 for profiling; long-term we should expose that window as a CLI arg for our infer binary.
Maya: and add a small wrapper that warmed KV cache with a few short sequences before capture so we avoid eviction noise.
Anna: repro steps I used (compact):
Anna: ```
export RED_SAMPLING_WINDOW=16
nsys profile -o tmp --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=25 ./run_inference.sh --concurrency 8 --requests 100
```
Anna: after that the timeline shows repeated tiny attention kernels and a clear correlation between kv-hit spikes and latency regression.
Ron: perfect. please file a perf ticket with the artifact link and mark as P2 — this is causing noisy regressions in canary.
Anna: filing now, attaching the capture and a tiny script to reproduce.
Sam: for future docs, let's add a short nsys checklist: 1) warm KV 2) duration >= 20s 3) set RED_SAMPLING_WINDOW if you expect <10ms kernels 4) consider --sample=none for full detail 5) trim traces with --filter-out if size too big
Maya: agreed. I'll add a short note to eng-runtime docs under profiling tips.
Anna: thanks — saved a lot of head-scratching. :thumbsup:
